summary: Oil. The topic of conversation almost every day, and for good reason. Crude prices are floating around $100 but far from the average of $65-75. Obviously, this is what pushed energy prices and inflation to be higher in the CPI report for August, but the core CPI, which excludes this noise, still increased. Meaning, there's second order inflation. Basically the oil shock is spilling over to input costs for companies which leads to higher prices for consumers and eventually a demand for higher wages. Also, after the Fed hike, the 10 year is floating near 5%, but what's more interesting is that the 2 year is around 4.77%. That's only a 21bps spread. Why does this matter? The 2 year measures what the Fed is expected to do in its future meetings, and it being this high means it expects the Fed to hike again. Looking at credit, the high yield OAS is surprisingly still tight at 268bps. So investors aren't demanding too much extra compensation for these companies. Also, another thing to look at → AI debt. Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon, and Oracle are issuing so much damn debt ($420 billion projected for 2027) that investors are now demanding more compensation for their bonds. This is a pretty cool mechanism to watch. These companies are investment grade, and the current average spread for investment-grade is 78 basis points. However, for these hyperscalers, the average is trading at 115bps spread. So investors are demanding more because their investments are all concentrated on AI companies, and they want to account for this risk even though these hyperscalers are financially super strong. Crazy that there's a bond oversupply right now. I might break my piggy bank early and hop on the train. Meta, get ready for my offer.

_oil_note: Optional daily override. Set asOf to the date you read them and fill wti/brent. Used only while newer than FRED's print - if you stop updating, it falls back to FRED automatically rather than showing an ever-staler number.
_curve_note: Optional hand entry for a yield FRED has not published yet. Same rule as oil: only used while newer than FRED. notes/alert are display only. Put alert on whatever the day's story is: it turns the figure rust and is the only thing telling a first-time visitor where to look. strain is the quieter version: a smaller crack on the summit, number stays in ink.
